extracted.intended_audience: governments, scientific experts, IPCC authors/reviewers, and stakeholders who use or contribute to IPCC assessments
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the IPCC's mission, organization, and the standards and procedures it uses to produce assessment reports — including evidence base, review and approval processes, working group mandates, and mechanisms for addressing errors and inclusion. Useful for people participating in, reviewing, or using IPCC reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: regular assessments of climate science, impacts, risks, adaptation and mitigation
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPCC provides regular assessments of the scientific basis of climate change, its impacts and future risks, and options for adaptation and mitigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Created in 1988 by WMO and UNEP, the objective of the IPCC is to provide governments at all levels with scientific information that they can use to develop climate policies. IPCC reports are also a key input into international climate change negotiations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence base: assess published literature; IPCC does not conduct original research
rubrics_metrics.description: For the assessment reports, experts volunteer their time as IPCC authors to assess the thousands of scientific papers published each year to provide a comprehensive summary of what is known about the drivers of climate change, its impacts and future risks, and how adaptation and mitigation can reduce those risks. The IPCC does not conduct its own research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPCC reports synthesize and evaluate existing scientific literature rather than producing new primary research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open and transparent review by experts and governments
rubrics_metrics.description: An open and transparent review by experts and governments around the world is an essential part of the IPCC process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The open review process is intended to ensure an objective and complete assessment and to reflect a diverse range of views and expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify strength of scientific agreement and highlight research needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Through its assessments, the IPCC identifies the strength of scientific agreement in different areas and indicates where further research is needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessments should distinguish levels of evidence and agreement, and explicitly point out gaps requiring additional research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author selection and contribution: governments and experts involvement
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPCC is an organization of governments that are members of the United Nations or WMO. Thousands of people from all over the world contribute to the work of the IPCC; experts volunteer as IPCC authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site provides fact sheets such as 'How does the IPCC select its authors?' and 'What is an Expert Reviewer of IPCC?' to explain selection and reviewer roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Working Group and Task Force mandates and topical scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPCC is divided into three Working Groups and a Task Force: Working Group I deals with The Physical Science Basis; Working Group II with Climate Change Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability; Working Group III with Mitigation of Climate Change. The Task Force on National Greenhouse Gas Inventories develops and refines methodology for the calculation and reporting of national greenhouse gas emissions and removals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other Task Groups may be established by the Panel for set time periods to consider specific topics or questions (e.g., a Task Group to improve gender balance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for report approval and for addressing alleged errors
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPCC has established processes for how it approves reports and how it deals with alleged errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site links to fact sheets 'How does the IPCC review process work', 'How does the IPCC approve reports', and 'How does the IPCC deal with alleged errors' for procedural detail and timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement, transparency and inclusivity (diverse participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are many ways to engage with the IPCC; the process aims to reflect a diverse range of views and expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information, fact sheets and translations are provided in multiple languages; the IPCC encourages participation by governments, experts and stakeholders and public engagement via social channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of targeted task groups to address specific issues (example: gender balance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Panel may establish Ad-hoc or Task Groups to consider a specific topic or question (example: the Task Group to improve gender balance established at the 47th Session).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task Group outputs can be fundamental to Panel decisions such as adopting a Gender Policy and Implementation Plan; such groups are time-limited and topic-focused.
